title: Dispatch: 7vh3 Conjure Elemental/Fey uncontrolled successor with cast-anchored 1-hour removal (Sonnet 5.5, attempt 1)
description:
Implement eshyra-7vh3 (read it: `bd show eshyra-7vh3`). Parent integration bead: eshyra-j3yp. All design decisions below are made; do not re-decide them. If something here contradicts the code or the SRD record text, stop and record the contradiction in your notes rather than improvising.

HARD RULE (bd memory srd-fidelity-hard-blocker): nothing may contradict the SRD. Source: packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json, records `spell:conjure-elemental` and `spell:conjure-fey` (`data.description`, `data.effects[0].transitions`). Do NOT edit records.json or any importer file.

## Source facts
"If your concentration is broken, the elemental doesn't disappear. Instead, you lose control of the elemental, it becomes hostile toward you and your companions, and it might attack. An uncontrolled elemental can't be dismissed by you, and it disappears 1 hour after you summoned it." (Conjure Fey identical for the fey creature.) Record transitions: `concentration-break-loss-of-control` (trigger concentration-broken: control->uncontrolled, attitude->hostile, restriction caster-cannot-dismiss, NO effect->ended), `cast-anchored-removal` (trigger absolute-time-reached, when control uncontrolled: effect->ended, presence->absent, timer {amount 1, unit hour, anchor spell-cast}), `zero-hp-removal` (applies controlled or uncontrolled). Duration "Concentration, up to 1 hour".

## Today
A concentration break ends the effect (`finalizeEnd`, packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts ~2480, mode 'break') and the record-derived cleanupOnBreak 'release' (deriveSummonCleanup ~2625) releases the actor link: the creature stays present but nothing ever removes it at cast+1h.

## Decision (captain, 2026-10-04): successor effect
Keep F3's terminal end semantics. When finalizeEnd ends a spell-sourced effect with reason 'concentration-broken' and the spell record (derive from transitions, NOT from spell names) has an `absolute-time-reached` transition that removes presence (presence->absent) with `when.control` 'uncontrolled', then in the SAME transaction, for the actor links that this break released, create one successor effect:
- effect_id `<original>:uncontrolled` (refuse/throw on collision rather than inventing another id), kind 'summoning', display_name `<original display_name> (uncontrolled)`, source kind 'spell' with the same source_ref and source actor, NO concentration (requires_concentration 0, no owner), NOT dismissible (source: "can't be dismissed by you"), status active.
- duration timed, amount 1, unit 'hour', and the ORIGINAL effect's anchor evidence copied verbatim (anchor kind, anchor_at, anchor_game_time, anchor_elapsed_minutes, and the deadline_elapsed_minutes = original anchor + 60). The record says cast-anchored: the deadline is 1 hour after the summoning, never 1 hour after the break. The original's declared duration already had to match "1 hour", so its world-time deadline equals the cast-anchored removal time; assert that (amount 1, unit hour) and fail closed otherwise. Round-unit or missing elapsed evidence -> fail closed with a clear error (do not guess).
- an active actor link for each released creature (same target_kind/target_ref/projection_ref/campaign_actor_id as the released link) with cleanup_on_end 'remove' and cleanup_on_break 'remove'; the creature also becomes a target if it was a target of the original.
- audit: the original's 'ended' event records the successor id; the successor's 'created' event records the predecessor id and the record transition id ('cast-anchored-removal'). Extend the typed event-detail validators rather than bypassing them.
The successor must not be created through the public createActiveEffect validation path that requires concentration for a "Concentration, up to" spell; write it through an internal path that still validates everything else. If validateActiveEffectDurableState or a strict read re-derives concentration from the spell record and would flag the successor, add an explicit durable marker (new migration `packages/core/data/migrations/00NN_*.sql` with the next free number, e.g. a nullable `predecessor_effect_id` column with a CHECK) and teach validation to accept exactly that case — never weaken the check for other effects.

Consequences that must then hold with no further special-casing (verify each in tests):
- advancing world time to the deadline (`advanceWorldTime` / `expireElapsedWorldEffects`) ends the successor 'expired' and its 'remove' cleanup makes the creature absent; one minute earlier it is still present; explicit `expired` before the deadline is refused.
- the creature dropping to 0 HP while uncontrolled still vanishes (closeActorLinkAtZeroHp finds the successor link) and the successor ends 'source-removed'.
- `end_effect` with 'dismissed' on the successor is refused (not dismissible); 'dispelled' / 'ruled' still work.
- the caster can start a new concentration effect (the successor holds no concentration).
- every concentration-break route produces the successor: failed damage save (resolveConcentrationCheck), incapacitation/death life-state hook, new-concentration replacement, voluntary break, and owner removal at combat closure if that route uses reason concentration-broken (check ~5199-5220 and closeCombatInstance; if combat closure releases the instance-only creature anyway, document what happens and test it).
- an ordinary end (expired at the 1-hour deadline while still controlled, dismissed) still removes the creature (existing derived cleanupOnEnd 'remove'); no successor.
- Spells whose break transition removes presence (e.g. Conjure Animals) are untouched: no successor.

## Model-facing text and docs
Update descriptions that state break/release behaviour (toolResolveConcentration.ts, toolEndEffect.ts, toolStartEffect.ts and any result text that reports cleanup actions) so the model learns that a broken concentration on Conjure Elemental/Fey leaves the creature present, uncontrolled and hostile under successor effect `<id>:uncontrolled`, which removes it 1 hour after it was summoned and which the caster cannot dismiss. Results that report the break should name the successor id. docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md: update §2 (the "Conjure Elemental distinction"), §4/§9 (S1 summons: the cast-anchored removal is executed) and remove the "not yet" wording. Re-derive every sentence against the source text and the real tool contract.

## Evidence
Add tests (packages/core/test/zeroHpVanishAndRemovePolicy.test.ts or a sibling `conjureUncontrolledRemoval.test.ts`; look at activeEffects.test.ts helpers for world-clock setup) asserting identities and exact values: successor id, kind, no concentration, dismissible false, deadline_elapsed_minutes = original anchor + 60 (create the effect, advance 20 minutes, break concentration, check the deadline is still anchor+60, not break+60), expiry at exactly the deadline makes the creature absent, 59 minutes after the summoning it is still present, 0-HP vanish ends the successor, dismissal refused, Conjure Fey parity, Conjure Animals unchanged, each break route above. No count-pinned assertions.

## Procedure
Work only in this worktree. Run `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing (it rewrites files); it must be fully green (documented skips only). Commit on this branch with a message starting `eshyra-7vh3`, ending with the line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
notes:
Completed on branch eshyra-j3yp.2. activeEffects.ts: finalizeEnd (break mode) calls new createUncontrolledSuccessor after cleanupOwnedState; derives the transition from the record (absolute-time-reached, presence->absent, when.control only 'uncontrolled', timer) via extended recordTransitions (whenControl, timer); fails closed if original duration/anchor/elapsed evidence != record timer; throws on id collision; writes through internal SQL (not createActiveEffect); EffectCleanupSummary.successorEffectId; ended event gets successorEffectId, successor created event gets predecessorEffectId + recordTransitionId. No migration needed (durable validation never re-derives concentration from the record). Tool descriptions (end_effect, start_effect, resolve_concentration) and docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md (§2, §9) updated. New test file packages/core/test/conjureUncontrolledRemoval.test.ts (14 tests: Elemental/Fey parity, exact deadline anchor+60 after break at +20, 59min alive/60 absent, early expired refused, 0HP vanish, dismissal refused/dispelled/ruled ok, new concentration allowed, ordinary end no successor, Conjure Animals none, id collision, routes: failed save, caster death, replacement, combat closure). Two existing tests updated (activeEffects.test.ts release-on-break: released creature can no longer be re-owned by a new effect, it is owned by the successor; zeroHpVanishAndRemovePolicy: vanished.effectId is now fx:uncontrolled). Combat closure note: a creature with a durable campaign-actor identity has the successor link rebound to the campaign actor and is still removed at cast+1h (tested); an instance-only creature link is released at closure per existing behaviour (successor then has no live link). Verification: npm run verify:worktree fully green (325 files passed, 2 skipped; 5895 tests passed, 3 skipped). Deviations: none.
Captain review fix (2026-10-04): the successor creation threw inside the concentration break when the original anchor was not exactly 'spell-cast' (start_effect also admits 'effect-created' and 'trigger-occurred' for hour timers), which would roll back the write that broke concentration (e.g. the caster's damage). Fixed: createActiveEffect now gates such spells to a 1-hour timer anchored to 'spell-cast' or 'effect-created' (SUMMONING_MOMENT_ANCHORS), and the break-time check accepts both. Tests added in conjureUncontrolledRemoval.test.ts; docs and start_effect text updated.
